newsitem.title: USA: Clinton urged by U.S. senators to isolate Iran.
newsitem.headline: Clinton urged by U.S. senators to isolate Iran.

text.p: A group of senators, including Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott, urged President Bill Clinton in a letter released on Friday to intensify U.S. efforts to isolate Iran.

"We urge you to maintain and intensify your efforts to isolate the Iranian regime through diplomacy and multilateral fora, since there is simply no reasonable cause to believe this regime can be reformed from within," they said in the letter to Clinton, signed by 10 senators and dated Feb. 10.

The senators said they held the Tehran government responsible for "its use of terrorism as a tool of foreign policy, its efforts to subvert neighbouring governments, its violent opposition to the Middle East peace process, its pursuit of a clandestine nuclear weapons programme, and its abysmal human rights record."

They urged Clinton, in crafting any new measures, to "draw a very clear distinction between the regime and the people of Iran" to make it clear that U.S. policy was aimed at changing the government's behaviour and not at penalising the people.
The senators, seven Republicans and three Democrats, said Clinton should put "support for democracy and human rights" at the centre of his Iran policy.

One of the Republicans, Sen. Alfonse D'Amato of New York, said legislation enacted last year to give the president authority to impose economic sanctions on any company that invests in the Iranian or Libyan oil industries appeared to be having an effect.
Iranian President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani said this week he could not foresee any easing in strained relations with the United States.
"The situation between us and America has not changed in several years and I do not see any other prospects in the future," Rafsanjani said in Tehran on Wednesday.
Iran has repeatedly asked the United States to release its frozen assets in U.S. banks which it estimates at about $12 billion.

The United States froze the assets, which it estimates in the hundred of millions of dollars, after the 1979 Islamic revolution when militants seized the U.S. embassy in Tehran and took its staff hostage.

The United States has launched a campaign to isolate Iran, accusing it of supporting terrorism and seeking to obtain nuclear weapons. Iran denies the charges and accuses the United States of aiming to destroy its Islamic government.
